# Phase 34.4 native-host scripted answers

Use equivalent briefs under `claude -p` and `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`.
When the inherited approval mode is automatic review, use `codex exec --approve-for-me`
instead: this CLI option itself selects workspace-write plus automatic review and
is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox`. Record the resolved authority and each review.
Each arm starts in a fresh scratch repository. Record the exact executable, version,
argv, source commit, plugin manifest digest, scratch identity, and `AuthorityEnvelope`.
The authority is filesystem `workspace-write`, network `inherited`, approvals `inherited`.
Permission or sandbox bypass options are forbidden. Do not widen inherited authority,
write outside scratch, contact product remotes, or perform unrecorded external actions.

## Common answers

Project: greenfield-proof. TypeScript library/CLI; npm; mobile: none; non-Blade.
Audience: developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI. The first
release exports a typed greeting and CLI with passing tests. No authentication,
external service, deployment, or product remote. Preserve unknowns explicitly.
Use the installed greenfield and roadmap plugin contracts and library-cli manifest.
Read the templates and references; do not substitute invented config keys or omit
promised homes. Existing brownfield homes and generated harness blocks are immutable.

## First invocation: proposal only

Read the fixture and run only the named `roadmap config capabilities --json`
compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including
`roadmap init --help`, before approval. Read static source or top-level help for
syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one
JSON object `{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[],"commands":[],"gates":{}}` with
concrete populated values. Its gates have exactly lint, types, unit, integration,
build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has
a reason. Validate those keys before requesting approval. Do not emit an approval
event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

The command plan is executable evidence. Each `commands` entry has the exact
absolute scratch `cwd`, a complete shell `command`, and an explicit `network`
description. Include full heredoc contents, generator/install/init calls, checks,
and wrapped gates; no pseudocode, omitted writer bodies, or placeholders. The
seven proposed gate strings must exactly match the config produced after approval.
During execution, run every planned shell command exactly once, in proposal order, and successfully,
with `cd '<scratch>' &&` followed by the unchanged proposed command. Do not add
shell discovery/checks or combine/split approved commands. Put discovery before
proposal or in the separate read-only audit. Read/Glob/Grep tools may inspect files.
All writes must use the explicitly proposed shell commands through Bash or
exec_command; Write, Edit, apply_patch, and other implicit file mutation tools are
not part of this trial's approved execution protocol. New-file writers use exclusive
creation; edits verify approved before-digests and reject unsafe/symlink targets.

For Codex execution, use direct `exec_command` calls or only this orchestration
form, with strict JSON argument objects: `text(await tools.exec_command({...}));`.
Use one call per envelope, quoted JSON keys, and no variables, aliases, other tools,
or arbitrary JavaScript. If polling is needed, the only other permitted envelope
is `text(await tools.write_stdin({...}));` with empty `chars`; it cannot send input.
The actual `cmd` is the exact proposed command with the explicit scratch cwd prefix.
Set `workdir` to scratch; do not request a custom shell or a TTY.
A required scoped automatic-review request may use `sandbox_permissions` and its
justification in that JSON object; it may not widen the requested operation.

## Driver approval and execution

The driver checks the complete proposal and unchanged initial tree, then records the
approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.
Resume the same host session with that exact standalone input. The prior proposal
is the approved path/command allowlist; do not bundle new instructions into approval.
If the proposal fails validation, issue no approval and capture the failed arm.
If any preapproval mutation occurs, STOP immediately without deleting or reverting
it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

Execute only approved operations. Emit `WRITE:` prose diagnostics for traceability (not extra shell calls), but
success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately with explicit `cd '<scratch>' &&` cwd evidence.
Use the host envelope below for suite/build/type commands; retain both the exact
portable configured command and the wrapped native invocation with its real exit. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

Required empty artifacts include PRD, both ADRs, CODE-STYLE, architecture index,
UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff
to approved gaps. Test migrated docs/roadmap, explicit root override, and ambiguous
dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

## Repeated invocation

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result
`{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only if the audit
finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.
Pass `sourceRoot`, `invocationBaseCommit`, and `sourceSnapshotSha256` in every
observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.
Use `greenfield-native-observer.py` in the same directory to launch each request;
it checks source before and after and records transient filesystem mutations.
Keep `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so read-only Git inspection does not refresh the index.
Propose scratch-local `.npm-cache/` and `.npm-logs/` paths when npm needs them;
include those settings in approved commands. Do not commit inside native fixtures.

After each stage finishes, run `greenfield-native-driver.mjs capture <host>
<stage-directory>` before resuming. The driver copies the native session and
checks identity, authority, command events, snapshots, and proposal structure.
Use separate `proposal`, `execution`, and `rerun` directories below each arm's
`dry-runs/evidence/` directory; never overwrite a failed attempt. Supply `arm.json`
with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

## Host build envelope

Resolve `/home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild` and its canonical path before launch;
bind its SHA-256, default limits, and permitted host effects as `gateWrapper` in
arm metadata and every stage request. Use the same binding for all four arms.
Keep `capbuild` out of consumer `gateCommands`; it is a host execution requirement,
not consumer tooling. For each build, type, unit, integration, and emit command,
propose its actual execution separately using this exact envelope:

```sh
cd '<scratch>' && /home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild --env npm_config_cache=<scratch>/.npm-cache --env npm_config_logs_dir=<scratch>/.npm-logs <configured-command>
```

Define `<scratch>` as the absolute observed fixture root and `<configured-command>`
as its exact portable gate binding. Use literal absolute cache/log values. Select
portable gate commands without shell operators or assignment prefixes; use
`env TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 node --import tsx roadmap/lib/emit.ts` for the fixture emit
gate so transform caching stays disabled across the systemd environment boundary.
Do not change memory/swap/heap/slice defaults, disable locks, add arbitrary environment
options, or run an unwrapped suite inside a compound verification command. Keep
config check and the selected catalog comparator as separate ordinary invocations.

Permit only capbuild's inherited host-control effects outside the consumer tree:
transient user-systemd units and `/run/user/<uid>/capbuild-locks`, where `<uid>` is
the current numeric user id recorded by the driver. These are safety metadata;
they do not authorize any additional consumer path. Record the actual wrapper
command/output/exit and verify the bound executable digest remains unchanged.
The observer clears ambient capbuild, Node, and forwarded test overrides before
launch and records the cleared variable names without exposing their values.

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

# zeroh-roadmap: Phase-Driven Development

Route ALL development work through the phase system — never create files/schemas/structure
ad hoc (honor-system). Invoke the CLI as `roadmap <cmd>` (fallback `node
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/roadmap.mjs <cmd>`).

**Layout — the ONE rule about paths.** The root is DISCOVERED (`roadmap/` or `docs/roadmap/`;
`ROADMAP_ROOT` overrides; both = refused), so **write `<root>/…`, never a bare `roadmap/…`** — a
path asserted as fact is wrong in the other layout. `roadmap init [--root <dir>]` is the ONLY
sanctioned initialization path. Mechanics: `references/layout.md`.

## Routing — what the user says → what you invoke

| User says | Invoke |
|---|---|
| create / plan phase, add to roadmap | **plan-phase** |
| do / start / execute phase N | **do-phase** |
| review / verify / check phase N | **review-phase** |
| plan / create / new arc | **plan-arc** |
| do / execute / run arc | **do-arc** |
| arc sweep, pre-merge sweep | **arc-sweep** |
| release sweep, resolve release debts | **release-sweep** — manual-only; ask the user to run `/release-sweep` |
| validate arc, intent validation | **validate-arc** |
| arc landed / eval the arc | **eval-arc** (do-arc Step 9 auto-runs it) |
| show roadmap, backlog | `roadmap status` + `<root>/ROADMAP.md` |
| what's next, next phase | `roadmap status` → **do-phase** |
| code review (a diff) | the `code-reviewer` agent / the built-in review command |
| full code review, pre-release review | **full-code-review** |
| audit roadmap, roadmap health check | **audit-roadmap** |
| pause the arc | stop anywhere; files are the truth |
| resume / continue arc X | **do-arc** — `roadmap arc next` fast-forwards from disk |
| hand off / fresh session | **handoff** |
| migrate / upgrade roadmap | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/migrate/README.md` |

NEVER handle these yourself (honor-system) — the skills carry the full protocol; your job is correct
dispatch plus the coordination below.

## Multi-session coordination (shared repos)

- The COORDINATION BOARD is `<root>/backlog.ts`'s header (lane map + release plan) — read it
  FIRST on "what next".
- `roadmap claim` BEFORE authoring a phase number (CLI-enforced: creation is the lock
  across worktrees).
- `roadmap status` shows live lanes; `roadmap arm <id>` claims an arc lane (CLI-enforced:
  refuses a taken lane — honor the refusal, never take over another session's arc).
- Cross-arc lanes ARE the sanctioned parallel path — one arc per session, gated by
  `roadmap capacity`.
- Answer lane/backlog questions from `roadmap status` + the board — never session memory.
- A consumer CLAUDE.md restating this is a mirror; on drift the CLI's behavior wins.

## Cross-cutting standards — load the reference when the work produces the artifact

Load one yourself whenever routed-to work surfaces the artifact class and the target
skill has not already:

- Writing docs, code comments, or a decision record → `references/documentation-rules.md`
- Assigning a task's `testMode` or refusing a test → `references/test-worthiness.md`
- Splitting or placing a UI component (at planning time) → `references/component-structure.md`
- Introducing any external package/font/icon/image/snippet/model → `references/external-assets-licensing.md`
- Running this protocol on a non-Claude harness (Codex) → `references/codex-tools.md`
- Scaffolding a consumer, writing a phase file's import, or a root refusal → `references/layout.md`

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, run only that named roadmap command; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.
Ask for the CI provider and protected release environment. Retain an unselected
provider as unavailable; never invent credentials or approve a deployment.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.
4. `references/ci-release-strategy.md` for the selected adapter, exact inventory/test/build commands, CI lifecycle, report/coverage baselines, provider placeholders and preservation plan.
5. `references/pointers.md` for delivery/config paths and their copy/validate order.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
roadmap configuration, and all four delivery outputs before requesting approval.
Inspect existing workflow paths first. STOP on any collision until the complete
proposal names an explicit merge decision, the preserved jobs/markers and exact
delta. The subsequent exact approval token approves only that listed merge.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

Include the concrete `delivery` object specified in `references/pointers.md`; bind
its provider, adapter, four output paths, environment, collision decision and
validation commands before approval.

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Ask for the exact response `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN`.

STOP before any write or generator run unless that exact response follows the
complete proposal. Do not interpret partial agreement as approval. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
Treat this gate as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs`; other approval interpretation is honor-system.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Delivery

Copy the approved planner and workflows from the installed plugin templates,
write the approved delivery configuration and fill the selected environment.
Merge approved existing workflow jobs and markers; never overwrite them silently.
Follow `references/pointers.md` to bind README commands and the CI backstop.
Installation does not authorize publishing or deployment.

## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete. Validate the installed workflow YAML and
execute the installed delivery planner/workflow mutation suite, recording actual
commands and terminal test totals. Record optional actionlint path/version or
unavailability; it cannot replace mandatory validation.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.
# Brownfield marker table

Inspect every row. Evidence supports classification but absence never proves a stack.

| Artefact | Evidence glob | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package managers | `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, `pubspec.yaml`, `gradlew` | Present files identify installed package tooling; conflicting locks are partial or stale evidence. |
| Framework files | `next.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `vite.config.*` | Framework-owned configuration supports a candidate stack that stack-decision must confirm. |
| Monorepo tools | `nx.json`, `turbo.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json` | Existing workspace orchestration is preserved and linked. |
| Docs | `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Existing fact homes are inventoried before proposing a missing index or canon. |
| Harness files | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.codex/**`, `opencode.json` | Apply the harness inventory and generated-block preservation contract. |
| Roadmap config | `roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `roadmap/phases/`, `docs/roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `docs/roadmap/phases/`, the explicit `ROADMAP_ROOT` path | Existing roadmap configuration is merged, never reinitialized. |
| Superpowers directory | `.superpowers/`, `docs/superpowers/` | Existing planning artifacts are linked rather than duplicated. |
| Design-system files | `components.json`, `**/components.json`, `tokens/**`, `**/*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` | Registries and token homes are evidence for design reconciliation, not permission to invent values. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

Use this read-only invocation after resolving the two absolute paths from the
installed plugin inventory and consumer Git toplevel:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; import { join } from "node:path"; const { roadmapRoot } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.argv[1], "cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs"))); console.log(roadmapRoot(process.argv[2]));' <roadmap-plugin-root> <consumer-root>
```

`<roadmap-plugin-root>` is the installed zeroh-roadmap plugin directory;

## Determinism and completeness

Versioned manifests bind source SHA, tree, normalized sorted unique identities,
runner/build contract digest and inventory digest. Normalize Windows separators
to `/`; reject traversal, absolute paths and duplicate identities. Generate the
inventory afresh: renamed identities replace old names, deleted tests disappear
and therefore face the approved count baseline. Default weight is exactly 1;
round-robin count balancing is deterministic. One shard and more requested shards
than units are valid; clamp the latter to units and emit no empty shard. Input
permutation cannot change the manifest, shards or digest. Fan-in requires every
planned shard exactly once and its executed identity union exactly equal to the
inventory. Report paths/digests are retained, not accepted from a summary alone.

The engine parses JUnit XML, Flutter machine JSON lines, LCOV and JaCoCo XML with
separate parsers. Truncated/contradictory summaries, duplicate cases, hidden failed
or skipped cases, malformed coverage, unknown formats and missing outputs fail.
Coverage paths are remapped only through approved roots, then merged once by
canonical file/line (maximum hit count, never summing percentages). Coverage is a
line-coverage floor in version 1; branch/function percentages are not asserted.

Keep every attempt. The generated runner disables test retries. Bounded external
infrastructure retry allows at most `maxInfraRetries` (0 by default, at most 2),
requires explicit infrastructure code/reason and retains first-attempt evidence.
A required test failure remains blocking even if a rerun passes (flaky).
Quarantine requires owner, reason and unexpired expiry, and still blocks an
authoritative release. Missing first attempts or gaps in numbering fail. Upload
compact reports and raw failure diagnostics under `always()`, even on failed jobs.

`minTests`, `minUnits` and `coverageFloor` are approved baselines. During preparation,
the engine reads the previous baseline from the tracked delivery config at `BASE_SHA`:
push uses the event's previous-main SHA; manual full requires an explicit approved
`base_sha` input. Scheduled/local validation uses the current commit's first parent.
A nonempty base must be an exact ancestor preceding HEAD. Missing history fails;
a root commit or new-branch push can prove that no prior branch baseline exists.
The plan binds `{baseSha,baseline,baselineDigest,requestedDigest}` as
`adapterConfig.baselineReference`, carried through fan-in and release verification.
A changed baseline requires
`baselineApproval: {baseSha,previous,previousDigest,approvedDigest,owner,reason}`,
matching the derived previous baseline and proposed values. The approval's `previous`

# Layout — where a consumer's roadmap lives

The router (`SKILL.md`) carries the operative rule: the root is DISCOVERED, so never state a
roadmap path as a fact. This file is the mechanics, for scaffolding a consumer, writing a phase
file's import, or diagnosing a refusal.

## The root

Two candidates, in precedence order: `roadmap/` at the git toplevel (what every existing consumer
has) and `docs/roadmap/` (for a repo that keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders).

- A candidate is the root when it carries a MARKER: `roadmap.config.json` or `phases/`. An
  existing but unmarked directory is not one — a repo with a prose `docs/roadmap/` folder keeps
  reading its real `roadmap/`.
- `ROADMAP_ROOT` overrides both, absolute or relative to the repo, and is NOT probed for
  existence — an override names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
- BOTH marked is a REFUSAL that names both paths and the `ROADMAP_ROOT` remedy, never a silent
  pick: two roots means two backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories, and guessing
  one is how half a consumer's records go quietly unread.
- Neither marked resolves to `roadmap/`, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers what it always did.

One resolver owns this — `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs` (`roadmapRoot`, `roadmapRootRel`,
`consumerSchemaPath`), with a shell twin at `hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh` for the hooks. A scan
tripwire in `cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs` keeps every other source out of the business of
spelling the root.

## Records and the schema seam

`backlog.ts`, `ROADMAP.md`, `phases/`, `arcs/`, `archive/`, `.gate/` and `arc-evals/` all sit
under the root. The schema seam resolves root-first: `<root>/lib/schema.ts`, else the legacy
`<toplevel>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that existing consumers vendored. Both stay supported; a
missing seam is named with BOTH paths.

A phase file at `<root>/phases/` therefore imports `../lib/schema`, an arc file at `<root>/arcs/`
the same, and `<root>/backlog.ts` imports `./lib/schema`. Relative, so a consumer needs no
tsconfig `paths` alias.

## Scaffolding

`roadmap init [--root <dir>]` — `--root` is forwarded to `scripts/scaffold-roadmap.sh` and
defaults to `roadmap`. The scaffold refuses, naming both, rather than create a second root beside
an existing one. `--root` is deliberately NOT a config key: the config lives inside the root it
would have to name.

## Missing homes

Keep each caller's documented STOP or inference behavior. If zeroh-greenfield is not installed,
use `/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace`; then delegate home authoring and
roadmap pointer writes to `brownfield-audit`. Never create or author missing homes inline.
# Documentation rules

The one standard every doc-producing surface cites. A document that fails a rule is
edited or deleted, never explained.

## The four principles

1. **Clear and concise** — skimmable: headings, tables, bullets. No jargon, no walls
   of prose. A reader finds their answer by scanning, not reading.
2. **No duplication** — one source of truth per fact; hyperlink to it instead of
   restating it. A second copy is where staleness is born.
3. **Timeless** — concepts and patterns, never dates, version numbers, or volatile
   paths/line numbers that rot. If a fact will be false in a month, it belongs in a
   report, not a doc.
4. **Current** — an outdated doc causes more friction than a missing one. Touching a
   doc means leaving the WHOLE doc true; delete or fix stale text on sight.

## The decision bar

Docs describe the **as-built** architecture. A standalone decision record exists only
when the decision is CRITICAL — one of:

- a boundary contract (something another team or repo builds against),
- a security/privacy posture,
- expensive to reverse,

— or when the user explicitly says "document this". Every other choice lives in the
phase's `transparencyReport` and dies with the phase. An ordinary implementation
choice never mints a doc.

## Code comments are documentation too

The same bar applies in source: a comment states a non-obvious WHY in one line, or it does
not exist. Narration ("this loop now handles…"), process archaeology (phase numbers, dates,
review rounds), and restating what the code visibly does are deleted on sight — the diff
and the transparencyReport carry that story.

## Evidence is not documentation

Verification records, audit sweeps, fix logs, screenshots, parity captures: gate-report
and `transparencyReport` material. They prove work happened; they do not describe the
system. Nothing of that class lands under `docs/`.

## Examples

| Bad | Good |
| --- | --- |
| `DECISION-2026-07-14-retry-backoff.md` explaining a retry constant | the constant's own comment states the non-obvious WHY; the choice is in the transparencyReport |
| "As of v0.43.0 the console (see src/routes/console.ts:214)…" | "The console reads ledger and stores only" — the code is the line-number authority |
| A 300-line VERIFICATION.md of command outputs | the gate report carries the run; docs/ stays architecture |
# External-asset licensing

The org's ratified policy for anything external a phase brings in — packages, fonts,
icons, images, snippets, models. The stakes: the product ships as PAID commercial SaaS
with installable client artifacts, so an incompatible license is a legal defect, not a
style issue. A task introducing one NAMES its license and placement before a byte lands;
unknown fails closed.

## The tiers

| Tier | Licenses | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allowed anywhere | MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, CC0, Unlicense, OFL | any artifact |
| Conditional | CC-BY (BY only — no NC/ND variants) with the attribution SHIPPED | any artifact, with the attribution in place |
| Server-side ONLY | GPL, LGPL, MPL | backend/services only — NEVER a shipped client artifact |
| Banned everywhere | AGPL, any non-commercial or no-derivatives clause (CC-BY-NC / CC-BY-ND), "free for personal use", unknown/unlicensed | nowhere; fail closed |

The server-side-only line is DELIBERATELY stricter than common practice (MPL is widely
treated as web-safe): the ratified policy draws it at the shipped artifact, never soften
it in a plan.

## The placement test — what counts as a shipped client artifact

The web bundle, the Office add-in, the Teams zip, the SPFx package — anything a customer
installs or a browser downloads. Copyleft code in one of these is a distribution event;
on a server we operate, it is not.

## The protocol

- **Planning** — a task introducing an external dependency or asset names its license and
  its placement tier in the task text. No license named = the task is not plannable.
- **Execution** — before vendoring/installing, verify the license matches what the plan
  named (read the upstream LICENSE, not the README badge). A mismatch stops the task; the
  verified license and placement land in the task's transparencyReport.
- **Unknown or gray-zone** (dual-licensed, custom terms) — fail
  closed and escalate: a `software-architect` Decision Contract call, and AGPL-class or
  commercial-terms questions go to the USER — never resolved by an executor.
- **Attribution duty** — CC-BY and any license requiring notice ships its attribution IN
  the artifact (a visible credits surface or bundled notice file), not in a repo comment.

This is a planning/execution rule, not a scanner: the org deliberately runs no CI license
gate — the plan-time naming and review-time check are the control.

broke — do not infer it from an installed-plugin listing, which reports installation, not surfacing.

## Action vocabulary → Codex tools

| The skills say | On Codex |
|---|---|
| read a file / search the repo | your file-read and shell tools; reading is free, read widely |
| spawn a role / dispatch an agent | `spawn_agent` (needs `multi_agent`, below) — or the child-CLI route when the role's model is not yours |
| message a running agent, ask for a fix round | `followup_task` — it delivers, triggers a turn, and reloads an evicted child |
| wait for a spawned role | `wait_agent`, in bounded stretches of 5-10 min; it is an event subscription, so short polls buy nothing |
| run a suite / a gate slot | your shell tool, wrapped per the consumer's shared-host rules |

Subagent tools require the feature to be on in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[features]
multi_agent = true
```

Trust your actual tool list over this table when they disagree — which tools you get depends on
the multi-agent version your model preset selects.

- **Spawning**: give children a clean context with `spawn_agent {fork_turns: "none"}`; the default
  `"all"` copies your entire transcript into the child. Role files under `~/.codex/agents/` attach
  to isolated forks via `agent_type` on **Codex 0.145+ only** — this host is 0.144.5, so treat
  `agent_type` as unavailable until you have checked your own version.
- **Model names**: never copy a model id from a skill, a table, or an old session into
  `spawn_agent` without checking it against your current spawn allowlist.
- **Lifecycle**: V2 has no `close_agent`; finished children are evicted automatically.

## Filling a role you cannot run yourself

`MULTI-DRIVER.md` §1 is the role table: each protocol spawn point has a class, a model tier chain
and a fulfillment mode. `resolveRole(roleId, 'codex')` returns which model to ask and how to reach
it — you do not choose either:

- **`native`** — the model is your own: `spawn_agent`.
- **`child-cli`** — the model belongs to another driver. Launch it as a headless child with the
  prompt on stdin, argv from the registry (`cli/lib/drivers.mjs`) — for the Claude family that is
  `claude -p [--agents <json>]`. This is how a Codex session fills the architect role on its
  chain's FIRST tier, a Claude-family model — read the chain itself off `MULTI-DRIVER.md` §1,
  never off this page.
- **`inline`** — no separate model is reachable, so you run the role yourself. Legal for
  builder-class roles, and RECORDED as inline: label it as your own work and never present it as
  an independent review.

Record every firing into the phase's `executionResult.roles`, and record a substitution when a
tier was skipped. A role binding that is not recorded did not happen as far as the scorecard is
concerned.

## Environment

Detect the checkout shape with read-only git before any worktree or branch step:

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
```

`GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` → you are already in a linked worktree (skip creation). Empty `BRANCH` →
detached HEAD: commit, then report the branch name and message rather than pushing.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scaffold-roadmap.sh — Initialize phase-driven roadmap in a project
#
# Usage: scaffold-roadmap.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [--root <dir>]
#   --root defaults to `roadmap`; `--root docs/roadmap` puts the whole consumer under
#   docs/roadmap/ beside a sibling docs folder. Everything lands UNDER the root, including the
#   schema seam — which is what lets a phase file import `../lib/schema` relatively, with no
#   tsconfig path alias. The legacy toplevel `lib/roadmap/schema.ts` seam stays recognized by
#   cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs, so existing consumers are untouched.
#
# Creates (<root> = --root, default `roadmap`):
#   <root>/lib/schema.ts     — definePhase() + Zod shapes
#   <root>/lib/registry.ts   — Phase discovery (dynamic import + validation)
#   <root>/lib/emit.ts       — Registry emission (deterministic JSON + digest)
#   <root>/ROADMAP.md        — Validation gate + git strategy
#   <root>/backlog.ts        — Ordered execution queue
#   <root>/phases/           — Empty phases directory
#   reviews/releases/         — Release review reports directory
#   scripts/pre-review.sh     — Automated pre-review checks
#   scripts/build-dashboard.sh — Review dashboard HTML generator

set -euo pipefail

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="."
ROOT="roadmap"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      ROOT="${2:?--root needs a directory}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --root=*)
      ROOT="${1#--root=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      PROJECT_DIR="$1"
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

# REFUSE rather than create a second root. Two marked roots is the ambiguity
# cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs refuses to resolve, so scaffolding one into existence would hand the
# consumer a repo no command can read. A marker is roadmap.config.json or phases/ — the same
# two the resolver probes.
for candidate in roadmap docs/roadmap; do
  [ "$candidate" = "$ROOT" ] && continue
  if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/roadmap.config.json" ] || [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/phases" ]; then
    echo "scaffold-roadmap: $PROJECT_DIR already carries a roadmap root at $candidate — refusing to create a second one at $ROOT." >&2
    echo "  Two roots means two backlogs and two registries, and every command would refuse to pick between them. Scaffold into $candidate, or move it first." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "=== Scaffolding zeroh-roadmap in $PROJECT_DIR (root: $ROOT) ==="

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/phases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/reviews/releases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"

# Copy <root>/lib templates — schema, registry, emit. This is the seam a phase file reaches with
# a RELATIVE `../lib/schema`; no tsconfig `paths` alias is required of the consumer.
for lib_file in schema.ts registry.ts emit.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file" ]; then
    cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/$lib_file" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
    echo "  Created $ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
  else
    echo "  Skipped $ROOT/lib/$lib_file (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Copy ROADMAP.md
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/ROADMAP.md" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/ROADMAP.md (already exists)"
fi

# Copy backlog.ts (ordered execution queue)
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/backlog.ts" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/backlog.ts"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/backlog.ts (already exists)"
fi

# Scaffold roadmap/arcs/ (OPT-IN — arcs are optional; defineArc rides along via schema.ts).
# Deliberately NOT in audit REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: a repo without arcs is fully valid.
# The directory only, never an example arc file: anything landing here is a LIVE arc, so a
# copied example makes id A with phases [1] real in a consumer that has authored none.
# templates/example.arc.ts stays installed with the plugin as reference material.
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/arcs"

# Copy scripts
for script in pre-review.sh build-dashboard.sh generate-changelog-md.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
      cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script"
      echo "  Created scripts/$script"
    fi
  else
    echo "  Skipped scripts/$script (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Make shell scripts executable
chmod +x "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/"*.sh 2>/dev/null || true

# Wire the npm scripts the skills invoke. do-phase / plan-phase / full-code-review all run
# `<pm> emit:phases` to regenerate reviews/changelog.json; without this script the agent can't
# find it and skips the regen. Idempotent: existing scripts are left untouched.
if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" ]; then
  node - "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" "$ROOT" <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const path = process.argv[2];
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
pkg.scripts = pkg.scripts || {};
const root = process.argv[3];
const want = {
  'emit:phases': `tsx ${root}/lib/emit.ts`,
  'changelog:md': 'tsx scripts/generate-changelog-md.ts',
};
let changed = false;
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(want)) {
  if (!pkg.scripts[k]) { pkg.scripts[k] = v; changed = true; console.log('  Added package.json script: ' + k); }
  else { console.log('  Skipped package.json script ' + k + ' (already set)'); }
}
if (changed) fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
NODE
else
  echo "  No package.json found — add a script manually: \"emit:phases\": \"tsx $ROOT/lib/emit.ts\""
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Done ==="
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Ensure 'zod' + 'tsx' are in your devDependencies (the emit:phases script runs tsx)."
echo "  2. Regenerate the changelog to confirm wiring: <pm> run emit:phases"
echo "  3. Create your first phase: /plan-phase"
echo "  4. Execute it: /do-phase 1"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review automated checks — catches mechanical issues before agent review.
# Run: bash scripts/pre-review.sh <first-commit-sha>
#
# Eliminates 40-50% of typical agent findings (missing tests, banned patterns,
# duplicate utilities, orphaned @contract tags) at near-zero cost.

set -euo pipefail

BASE="${1:-HEAD~1}"
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m'

ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0

fail() { echo -e "${RED}FAIL:${NC} $1"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS+1)); }
warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}WARN:${NC} $1"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS+1)); }
pass() { echo -e "${GREEN}  OK:${NC} $1"; }

echo "=== Pre-Review Checks (diff from $BASE) ==="
echo

# ── 1. New lib/services/ files must have test files ───────────────────────────
echo "--- New service files need tests ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/services/*.ts' 'lib/business-rules/*.ts' | grep -v __tests__); do
  basename=$(basename "$f" .ts)
  dir=$(dirname "$f")
  test_file="$dir/__tests__/$basename.test.ts"
  if [ -f "$test_file" ]; then
    pass "$f → $test_file exists"
  else
    fail "$f has no test file at $test_file"
  fi
done

# ── 2. No fs.readFileSync in API routes ───────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- No fs.readFileSync in API routes ---"
if grep -rn "fs\.readFileSync\|fs\.readFile\b" app/api/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "fs.readFileSync in API route — use import for JSON (standalone build won't bundle runtime reads)"
else
  pass "No fs.readFileSync in API routes"
fi

# ── 3. No toBeCloseTo on exact arithmetic ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check toBeCloseTo usage ---"
matches=$(grep -rn "toBeCloseTo" lib/**/__tests__/*.ts 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
  warn "toBeCloseTo found — verify these aren't masking rounding bugs on exact values:"
  echo "$matches" | head -5
else
  pass "No toBeCloseTo in service tests"
fi

# ── 4. @contract tags have @spec tests ────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- @contract tags have @spec coverage ---"
if [ -f "compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts" ]; then
  if npx tsx compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "@contract/@spec alignment verified"
  else
    fail "Orphaned @contract tags without @spec tests"
  fi
else
  pass "@contract spec check script not found (skipped)"
fi

# ── 5. New @contract tags in diff ─────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- New @contract tags ---"
new_tags=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/' | grep "^+" | grep "@contract" | grep -v "^+++" || true)
if [ -n "$new_tags" ]; then
  warn "New @contract tags added — verify relationship and confidence:"
  echo "$new_tags" | head -10
fi

# ── 6. No duplicate utility functions ─────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check for duplicate utilities ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | grep -v __tests__ | grep -v node_modules); do
  # Extract new function names
  new_fns=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- "$f" | grep "^+.*function " | sed 's/.*function \([a-zA-Z_]*\).*/\1/' | grep -v "^$" || true)
  for fn in $new_fns; do
    # Check if function name exists elsewhere in lib/utils/ or lib/services/
    existing=$(grep -rn "function $fn\b" lib/utils/ lib/services/ --include="*.ts" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
      warn "Function '$fn' in $f may duplicate: $existing"
    fi
  done
done

# ── 7. DB queries outside try/catch in API routes ─────────────────────────────
echo "--- DB queries in API routes ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'app/api/**/route.ts'); do
  if grep -q "await db\." "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Check if there's a try/catch wrapping it
    if ! grep -q "try {" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
      fail "$f has DB queries without try/catch"
    else
      pass "$f has DB queries with try/catch"
    fi
  fi
done

# ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo
echo "=== Summary ==="
echo -e "Errors: ${RED}${ERRORS}${NC}  Warnings: ${YELLOW}${WARNINGS}${NC}"
if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}Fix errors before running agent review.${NC}"
  exit 1
else
  echo -e "${GREEN}Pre-review checks passed.${NC}"
  exit 0
fi

const REVIEW_DATA = """ + reviews_json + r""";

function esc(s) {
  return String(s == null ? '' : s)
    .replace(/&/g, '&')
    .replace(/</g, '<')
    .replace(/>/g, '>')
    .replace(/"/g, '"');
}

function renderDashboard(data) {
  const sorted = [...data].sort((a, b) => b.version.localeCompare(a.version));
  const labels = [...sorted].reverse().map(r => 'v' + r.version);
  const unitCounts  = [...sorted].reverse().map(r => r.gate && r.gate.unitTests && r.gate.unitTests.passed != null ? r.gate.unitTests.passed : 0);

    options: {
      responsive: true,
      maintainAspectRatio: false,
      plugins: { legend: baseLegend },
      scales: {
        x: { ticks: { color: '#8db8a0' }, grid: { color: 'rgba(30,64,48,0.5)' } },
        y: {
          type: 'linear',
          position: 'left',
          title: { display: true, text: 'Unit Tests', color: '#3a9e63', font: { size: 11 } },
          ticks: { color: '#3a9e63' },
          grid: { color: 'rgba(30,64,48,0.5)' }

          ticks: { color: '#3498db' },
          grid: { drawOnChartArea: false }

      labels,

    options: { responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false, plugins: { legend: baseLegend }, scales: baseScales }

  sorted.forEach(function(review) {

    card.className = 'version-card';

    const verdict = (review.verdict || 'PASSED').toUpperCase();
    const phaseCount   = (review.phases || []).length;
    const findingCount = (review.findings || []).length;
    const verdictClass = (verdict === 'PASSED' || verdict === 'RELEASED') ? 'passed' : 'failed';

    const meta = [
      review.date,
      phaseCount  ? phaseCount  + ' phase'   + (phaseCount  !== 1 ? 's' : '') : null,
      findingCount ? findingCount + ' finding' + (findingCount !== 1 ? 's' : '') : null
    ].filter(Boolean).join(' · ');

    const header = document.createElement('div');
    header.className = 'version-header';
    header.innerHTML =
      '<span class="verdict-badge ' + verdictClass + '">' + verdict + '</span>' +
      '<span class="version-title">v' + esc(review.version) + '</span>' +
      '<span class="version-meta">' + esc(meta) + '</span>' +
      '<span class="chevron">›</span>';

    const body = document.createElement('div');
    body.className = 'version-body';

    // Gate results
    const gate = review.gate || {};
    function gateItem(label, value) {
      if (value == null) return '<div class="gate-item"><div class="gate-label">' + esc(label) + '</div><div class="gate-value unknown">\u2014</div></div>';
      const s = String(value);
      const isGreen = s === 'clean' || /^\d+\/\d+$/.test(s);
      return '<div class="gate-item"><div class="gate-label">' + esc(label) + '</div><div class="gate-value' + (isGreen ? ' clean' : '') + '">' + esc(s) + '</div></div>';
    }
    function testsLabel(obj) {
      if (!obj) return null;
      if (obj.passed != null) return obj.passed + '/' + obj.total;
      return null;
    }

    let html = '<div class="gate-grid">';
    html += gateItem('Lint', gate.lint);
    html += gateItem('Type Check', gate.typeCheck);

        const vClass = totalF === 0 ? '' : ' has-findings';
        const phaseLabel = r.phase ? ' (phase ' + r.phase + ')' : '';
        const agentSummary = (r.agents || []).map(function(a) { return a.name + ': ' + a.findings; }).join(', ');
        html += '<div class="round-row">';
        html += '<span class="round-label">Round ' + r.round + esc(phaseLabel) + '</span>';
        html += '<span class="round-verdict' + vClass + '">' + esc(r.verdict || agentSummary) + '</span>';
        html += '</div>';
      });
      html += '</div>';

    // Phases
    if (review.phases && review.phases.length > 0) {
      html += '<div class="phases-list"><h4>Phases Included</h4>';
      review.phases.forEach(function(p) {

    if (review.findings && review.findings.length > 0) {

function formatDate(isoDate: string): string {
  if (!isoDate) return ''
  const d = new Date(isoDate)
  return d.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' })
}

function renderSection(title: string, entries: ChangelogEntry[]): string {
  if (entries.length === 0) return ''
  const items = entries.map((e) => `- **${e.name}** — ${e.description}`).join('\n')
  return `### ${title}\n\n${items}\n`
}

function generate() {
  if (!fs.existsSync(CHANGELOG_JSON)) {
    console.error(`ERROR: ${CHANGELOG_JSON} not found. Run the configured emit gate (or the emit:phases package script) first.`)
    process.exit(1)
  }

  const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(CHANGELOG_JSON, 'utf-8')) as {
    versions: ChangelogVersion[]
  }

  const lines: string[] = [
    '---',
    'sidebar_position: 99',
    'title: Changelog',
    '---',
    '',
    '<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-changelog-md.ts from reviews/changelog.json; run the changelog:md package script to regenerate. -->',
    '',
    '# Changelog',
    '',
    'All notable changes to this project.',
    '',
    '---',
    '',
  ]

  for (const ver of data.versions) {
    const dateStr = ver.date ? ` — ${formatDate(ver.date)}` : ''
    lines.push(`## v${ver.version}${dateStr}`)
    lines.push('')

    const features = renderSection("What's New", ver.sections.features)
    const fixes = renderSection('Fixed', ver.sections.fixes)
    const internal = renderSection('Under the Hood', ver.sections.internal)

    if (features) lines.push(features)
    if (fixes) lines.push(fixes)
    if (internal) lines.push(internal)

    lines.push('---')
    lines.push('')
  }

  const content = lines.join('\n')
  fs.writeFileSync(CHANGELOG_MD, content)
  console.log(`Generated: ${CHANGELOG_MD}`)
  console.log(`  ${data.versions.length} versions`)
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-review automated checks — catches mechanical issues before agent review.
# Run: bash scripts/pre-review.sh <first-commit-sha>
#
# Eliminates 40-50% of typical agent findings (missing tests, banned patterns,
# duplicate utilities, orphaned @contract tags) at near-zero cost.

set -euo pipefail

BASE="${1:-HEAD~1}"
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m'

ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0

fail() { echo -e "${RED}FAIL:${NC} $1"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS+1)); }
warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}WARN:${NC} $1"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS+1)); }
pass() { echo -e "${GREEN}  OK:${NC} $1"; }

echo "=== Pre-Review Checks (diff from $BASE) ==="
echo

# ── 1. New lib/services/ files must have test files ───────────────────────────
echo "--- New service files need tests ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/services/*.ts' 'lib/business-rules/*.ts' | grep -v __tests__); do
  basename=$(basename "$f" .ts)
  dir=$(dirname "$f")
  test_file="$dir/__tests__/$basename.test.ts"
  if [ -f "$test_file" ]; then
    pass "$f → $test_file exists"
  else
    fail "$f has no test file at $test_file"
  fi
done

# ── 2. No fs.readFileSync in API routes ───────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- No fs.readFileSync in API routes ---"
if grep -rn "fs\.readFileSync\|fs\.readFile\b" app/api/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "fs.readFileSync in API route — use import for JSON (standalone build won't bundle runtime reads)"
else
  pass "No fs.readFileSync in API routes"
fi

# ── 3. No toBeCloseTo on exact arithmetic ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check toBeCloseTo usage ---"
matches=$(grep -rn "toBeCloseTo" lib/**/__tests__/*.ts 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
  warn "toBeCloseTo found — verify these aren't masking rounding bugs on exact values:"
  echo "$matches" | head -5
else
  pass "No toBeCloseTo in service tests"
fi

# ── 4. @contract tags have @spec tests ────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- @contract tags have @spec coverage ---"
if [ -f "compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts" ]; then
  if npx tsx compliance/scripts/check-contract-specs.ts 2>/dev/null; then
    pass "@contract/@spec alignment verified"
  else
    fail "Orphaned @contract tags without @spec tests"
  fi
else
  pass "@contract spec check script not found (skipped)"
fi

# ── 5. New @contract tags in diff ─────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- New @contract tags ---"
new_tags=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'lib/' | grep "^+" | grep "@contract" | grep -v "^+++" || true)
if [ -n "$new_tags" ]; then
  warn "New @contract tags added — verify relationship and confidence:"
  echo "$new_tags" | head -10
fi

# ── 6. No duplicate utility functions ─────────────────────────────────────────
echo "--- Check for duplicate utilities ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' | grep -v __tests__ | grep -v node_modules); do
  # Extract new function names
  new_fns=$(git diff "$BASE"..HEAD -- "$f" | grep "^+.*function " | sed 's/.*function \([a-zA-Z_]*\).*/\1/' | grep -v "^$" || true)
  for fn in $new_fns; do
    # Check if function name exists elsewhere in lib/utils/ or lib/services/
    existing=$(grep -rn "function $fn\b" lib/utils/ lib/services/ --include="*.ts" 2>/dev/null | grep -v "$f" | head -1 || true)
    if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
      warn "Function '$fn' in $f may duplicate: $existing"
    fi
  done
done

# ── 7. DB queries outside try/catch in API routes ─────────────────────────────
echo "--- DB queries in API routes ---"
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$BASE"..HEAD -- 'app/api/**/route.ts'); do
  if grep -q "await db\." "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Check if there's a try/catch wrapping it
    if ! grep -q "try {" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then
      fail "$f has DB queries without try/catch"
    else
      pass "$f has DB queries with try/catch"
    fi
  fi
done

# ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo
echo "=== Summary ==="
echo -e "Errors: ${RED}${ERRORS}${NC}  Warnings: ${YELLOW}${WARNINGS}${NC}"
if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}Fix errors before running agent review.${NC}"
  exit 1
else
  echo -e "${GREEN}Pre-review checks passed.${NC}"
  exit 0
fi

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}
